Tariq_Rahman/Pakistan_s_Wars__An_Alterna.author: Tariq Rahman
Tariq_Rahman/Pakistan_s_Wars__An_Alterna.title: Pakistan's Wars: An Alternative History
Tariq_Rahman/Pakistan_s_Wars__An_Alterna.summary: Tariq Rahman's Pakistan's Wars: An Alternative History reconstructs the major Pakistani wars (1947-48, 1965, 1971, Kargil 1999, post-9/11 frontier wars) from a non-establishment Pakistani perspective, drawing on Urdu memoirs and Pakistani veteran testimony. Field sites: Punjab, Kashmir LoC, FATA. Methodology: synthetic military-political history. Published 2022 by Vanguard Books.

Victoria_Schofield/Afghan_Frontier__Feud.author: Victoria Schofield
Victoria_Schofield/Afghan_Frontier__Feud.title: Afghan Frontier: Feuding and Fighting in Central Asia
Victoria_Schofield/Afghan_Frontier__Feud.summary: Victoria Schofield's Afghan Frontier traces 200 years of Anglo-Afghan and Anglo-Russian rivalry in Afghanistan and the Pashtun frontier, drawing on British archival sources and Schofield's earlier reportage in Pakistan. Field sites: Khyber, eastern Afghanistan, NWFP. Methodology: narrative history. Published 2003 by I.B. Tauris.

Victoria_W_Miroshnik/How_Pakistan_Was_Fo.author: Victoria W. Miroshnik
Victoria_W_Miroshnik/How_Pakistan_Was_Fo.title: How Pakistan Was Formed: The Economic Rationale for Partition
Victoria_W_Miroshnik/How_Pakistan_Was_Fo.summary: Victoria W Miroshnik's 'How Pakistan Was Formed: The Economic Rationale for Partition' is a religious-studies monograph on agrarian and pastoral life, gender and women's experience, and kinship and family. Regional focus: Pakistan. From the opening: 'The nephew of Raja Dahir, his warriors and principal officers have been dispatched, and the infidels converted to Islam or destroyed.' Field site: Jammu, Sindh, Hyderabad, Lahore District. Published 2019.

William_Maley/The_Afghanistan_Wars__e090.author: William Maley
William_Maley/The_Afghanistan_Wars__e090.title: The Afghanistan Wars
William_Maley/The_Afghanistan_Wars__e090.summary: William Maley's 'The Afghanistan Wars' is a historical monograph on agrarian and pastoral life, ethnicity and identity politics, and gender and women's experience. Regional focus: Afghanistan, Pakistan. From the opening: 'It maintained its neutrality during the Second World War, avoided war with its neighbours, and was internally free of mass killings and mayhem.' Field site: Kabul, Kandahār, Peshawar Division, Hazāras. Published 2002 by Palgrave Macmillan.

Zhanhuan_Shang/Carbon_Management_for_Pro.author: Zhanhuan Shang
Zhanhuan_Shang/Carbon_Management_for_Pro.title: Carbon Management for Promoting Local Livelihood in the Hindu Kush Himalayan: HKH: Region
Zhanhuan_Shang/Carbon_Management_for_Pro.summary: Zhanhuan Shang's 'Carbon Management for Promoting Local Livelihood in the Hindu Kush Himalayan: HKH: Region 1st ed' is an economic monograph on agrarian and pastoral life, politics and conflict, and religion and ritual. Regional focus: Pakistan. From the opening: 'COP24 confer- ence in Katowice, Poland, was the commitment of all contracting states to ‘nation- ally report greenhouse gas emissions and emission reduction efforts to establish a unified and transparent set of guidelines’.' Field site: Dharan. Published 2020 by Springer.

Saiba_Varma/The_Occupied_Clinic__bc34f6c.author: Saiba Varma
Saiba_Varma/The_Occupied_Clinic__bc34f6c.title: The Occupied Clinic: Militarism and Care in Kashmir
Saiba_Varma/The_Occupied_Clinic__bc34f6c.summary: Saiba Varma's The Occupied Clinic is an ethnography of psychiatric and medical care in the Kashmir Valley under Indian military occupation, arguing that medicine and militarism are co-constituted rather than separate domains. Drawing on long-term fieldwork in hospitals, clinics, and homes in Srinagar and surrounding districts, Varma shows how counterinsurgency reshapes how Kashmiris experience care, suffering, and trust. Field site: Srinagar and the Kashmir Valley, India-administered Jammu and Kashmir. Methodology: ethnographic fieldwork with patients, psychiatrists, and security personnel. Published 2020 by Duke University Press.

Naveeda_Khan/Muslim_Becoming_Aspiration_.author: Naveeda Khan
Naveeda_Khan/Muslim_Becoming_Aspiration_.title: Muslim Becoming: Aspiration and Skepticism in Pakistan
Naveeda_Khan/Muslim_Becoming_Aspiration_.summary: Naveeda Khan's Muslim Becoming examines theological argument and everyday Islam in urban Pakistan, arguing that ordinary Muslims approach faith through aspiration and skepticism rather than fixed doctrine. The book traces sectarian disputes and Sufi-influenced practice in Lahore and other Punjabi cities, drawing on extended ethnographic fieldwork and on close reading of Urdu polemical literature. Field site: Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan. Methodology: ethnographic fieldwork combined with vernacular textual analysis. Published 2012 by Duke University Press.

Hafsa_Kanjwal/Colonizing_Kashmir_State_B.author: Hafsa Kanjwal
Hafsa_Kanjwal/Colonizing_Kashmir_State_B.title: Colonizing Kashmir: State-Building under Indian Occupation
Hafsa_Kanjwal/Colonizing_Kashmir_State_B.summary: Hafsa Kanjwal's Colonizing Kashmir argues that postcolonial Indian rule in Jammu and Kashmir constitutes a settler-colonial project, with Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad's 1953-63 government as a constitutive phase of state-building. Based on archival research in Indian and Kashmiri archives plus oral histories, the book documents how infrastructure, tourism, education, and emergency law produced consent and coercion in the Valley. Field site: Srinagar, Kashmir Valley, and Indian state archives. Methodology: archival history with oral history interviews. Published 2023 by Stanford University Press.

Humeira_Iqtidar/Secularizing_Islamists_I.author: Humeira Iqtidar
Humeira_Iqtidar/Secularizing_Islamists_I.title: Secularizing Islamists? Jamaat-e-Islami and Jamaat-ud-Dawa in Urban Pakistan
Humeira_Iqtidar/Secularizing_Islamists_I.summary: Humeira Iqtidar's Secularizing Islamists argues that Pakistani Islamist parties Jamaat-e-Islami and Jamaat-ud-Dawa, far from being a counter-secular force, have themselves contributed to secularization in Lahore by detaching religion from custom and embedding it in state politics. The book draws on ethnographic fieldwork inside both organizations. Field site: Lahore, Pakistan. Methodology: ethnographic fieldwork with Islamist activists. Published 2011 by University of Chicago Press.

Cabeiri_Robinson/Body_of_Victim_Body_of_.author: Cabeiri deBergh Robinson
Cabeiri_Robinson/Body_of_Victim_Body_of_.title: Body of Victim, Body of Warrior: Refugee Families and the Making of Kashmiri Jihadists
Cabeiri_Robinson/Body_of_Victim_Body_of_.summary: Cabeiri D. Robinson's Body of Victim, Body of Warrior is an ethnography of Kashmiri refugee families in Azad Jammu and Kashmir whose sons have joined cross-LoC militant groups. Robinson argues that Kashmiri jihad must be understood through the moral economy of muhajir refugee status and family honor rather than through Pakistani state recruitment alone. Field site: Muzaffarabad and Mirpur, Azad Jammu and Kashmir. Methodology: long-term ethnographic fieldwork. Published 2013 by University of California Press.

Antonio_Giustozzi/Koran_Kalashnikov_Lapt.author: Antonio Giustozzi
Antonio_Giustozzi/Koran_Kalashnikov_Lapt.title: Koran, Kalashnikov, and Laptop: The Neo-Taliban Insurgency in Afghanistan
Antonio_Giustozzi/Koran_Kalashnikov_Lapt.summary: Antonio Giustozzi's Koran, Kalashnikov, and Laptop maps the rebuilding of the Taliban movement after 2001, tracing recruitment, financing, and tactical adaptation across southern and eastern Afghanistan. The book draws on field interviews with insurgent commanders and ANA personnel. Field sites: Kandahar, Helmand, Uruzgan, Zabul, eastern border provinces. Methodology: militant and security-source interviews. Published 2008 by Hurst.

David_B_Edwards/Heroes_of_the_Age_Moral_.author: David B. Edwards
David_B_Edwards/Heroes_of_the_Age_Moral_.title: Heroes of the Age: Moral Fault Lines on the Afghan Frontier
David_B_Edwards/Heroes_of_the_Age_Moral_.summary: David B. Edwards' Heroes of the Age is a foundational anthropological history of Afghan moral imagination centered on three iconic figures: a Pashtun tribal saint, an Amir, and a Marxist intellectual. Edwards argues that competing models of legitimate authority — tribe, state, and revolution — have structured Afghan political life since the late 19th century. Field sites: eastern Afghan/Pakistan borderland (Pukhtun tribal areas, Peshawar, Kabul). Methodology: ethnographic fieldwork combined with biographical history. Published 1996 by University of California Press.

Robert_Crews/Afghan_Modern_History_Globa.author: Robert D. Crews
Robert_Crews/Afghan_Modern_History_Globa.title: Afghan Modern History Global Nation
Robert_Crews/Afghan_Modern_History_Globa.summary: Robert Crews's 'Afghan Modern History Global Nation' is a historical monograph on agrarian and pastoral life, ethnicity and identity politics, and politics and conflict. Regional focus: Afghanistan, Pakistan. From the opening: 'Afghan diaspora abroad and the rulers of the kingdom in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, this chapter shows how Afghan nation-making was, at multiple levels, part of a series of global processes.' Field site: Kabul, Kandahār, Peshawar Division, Hazāras. Published 2015 by Harvard University Press.

Robert_Crews/Crews_Afghan_Modern__7067e9.author: Robert D. Crews
Robert_Crews/Crews_Afghan_Modern__7067e9.title: Afghan Modern: The History of a Global Nation
Robert_Crews/Crews_Afghan_Modern__7067e9.summary: Robert Crews's 'Crews Afghan Modern' is a historical monograph on agrarian and pastoral life, ethnicity and identity politics, and politics and conflict. Regional focus: Afghanistan, Pakistan. From the opening: 'Afghan diaspora abroad and the rulers of the kingdom in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, this chapter shows how Afghan nation-making was, at multiple levels, part of a series of global processes.' Field site: Kabul, Kandahār, Peshawar Division, Hazāras. Published 2015 by Harvard University Press.

Mike_Martin/Intimate_War_Helmand_Martin_.author: Mike Martin
Mike_Martin/Intimate_War_Helmand_Martin_.title: An Intimate War: An Oral History of the Helmand Conflict, 1978-2012
Mike_Martin/Intimate_War_Helmand_Martin_.summary: Mike Martin's An Intimate War is an oral history of the Helmand conflict from the 1978 communist coup through the 2012 NATO drawdown, drawing on Pashto-language interviews Martin conducted as a British army officer. The book argues that the conflict's drivers were intra-tribal and tribal-state rather than ideological, and that Western framings of 'Taliban' obscure this. Field site: Helmand Province, Afghanistan. Methodology: oral history with Helmandi informants. Published 2014 by Hurst.

Olivier_Roy/Islam_and_Resistance_in_Afgh.author: Olivier Roy
Olivier_Roy/Islam_and_Resistance_in_Afgh.title: Islam and Resistance in Afghanistan
Olivier_Roy/Islam_and_Resistance_in_Afgh.summary: Olivier Roy's Islam and Resistance in Afghanistan is the foundational political-anthropological account of the anti-Soviet mujahideen, arguing that the resistance was structured by older Sufi networks and tribal segmentation rather than by Islamist ideology imported from Egypt. Roy draws on extended fieldwork in Pakistan-based mujahideen camps and inside Afghanistan. Field sites: Peshawar mujahideen camps, eastern Afghan provinces (Nuristan, Kunar, Panjshir). Methodology: political ethnography. Published 1986 by Cambridge University Press.

Dipali_Mukhopadhyay/Warlords_Strongman_G.author: Dipali Mukhopadhyay
Dipali_Mukhopadhyay/Warlords_Strongman_G.title: Warlords, Strongman Governors, and the State in Afghanistan
Dipali_Mukhopadhyay/Warlords_Strongman_G.summary: Dipali Mukhopadhyay's Warlords, Strongman Governors, and the State in Afghanistan traces how former mujahideen and anti-Taliban militia leaders re-entered state office as provincial governors after 2001, arguing that these 'strongman governors' produced a hybrid order rather than obstructing state-building. Drawing on field interviews with governors including Atta Mohammad Noor (Balkh) and Gul Agha Sherzai (Nangarhar), the book argues for re-evaluating informal authority. Field sites: Mazar-i-Sharif (Balkh), Jalalabad (Nangarhar), Herat. Methodology: elite political ethnography. Published 2014 by Cambridge University Press.

Goldie_Osuri/Religious_Freedom_in_India_.author: Goldie Osuri
Goldie_Osuri/Religious_Freedom_in_India_.title: Religious Freedom in India: Sovereignty and (Anti) Conversion
Goldie_Osuri/Religious_Freedom_in_India_.summary: Goldie Osuri's Religious Freedom in India argues that anti-conversion debates and Hindutva mobilization reveal a fundamental Indian state ambivalence about minority religious sovereignty, with particular attention to Adivasi, Christian, and Kashmiri Muslim communities. The book combines critical theory with discourse analysis. Field sites: textual and policy; Indian-administered Kashmir as recurring case. Methodology: critical political theory. Published 2013 by Routledge.

Christopher_Snedden/Understanding_Kashmi.author: Christopher Snedden
Christopher_Snedden/Understanding_Kashmi.title: Understanding Kashmir and Kashmiris
Christopher_Snedden/Understanding_Kashmi.summary: Christopher Snedden's Understanding Kashmir and Kashmiris synthesizes the political, religious, and ethnic complexity of all the entities of the former princely state — Indian-administered J&K, Pakistan-administered Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan, and Chinese-controlled Aksai Chin and the Trans-Karakoram Tract. The book draws on extended fieldwork across the divided Kashmir region. Field sites: Srinagar, Jammu, Muzaffarabad, Gilgit, Skardu. Methodology: historical and political synthesis with interviews. Published 2015 by Hurst.

Suvir_Kaul/Suvir_Kaul_Of_Gardens_Graves_.author: Suvir Kaul
Suvir_Kaul/Suvir_Kaul_Of_Gardens_Graves_.title: Of Gardens and Graves: Kashmir, Poetry, Politics
Suvir_Kaul/Suvir_Kaul_Of_Gardens_Graves_.summary: Suvir Kaul's Of Gardens and Graves reads contemporary Kashmiri poetry and political essays as testimony to the everyday violence of Indian military occupation in the Kashmir Valley. The book translates and analyzes Kashmiri and Urdu poetry by writers such as Agha Shahid Ali, Naseem Shafaie, and others. Field site: Kashmir Valley (textual and visited). Methodology: literary criticism with political reflection. Published 2015 by Three Essays Collective.

Sumantra_Bose/Kashmir_Roots_of_Conflict_.author: Sumantra Bose
Sumantra_Bose/Kashmir_Roots_of_Conflict_.title: Kashmir: Roots of Conflict, Paths to Peace
Sumantra_Bose/Kashmir_Roots_of_Conflict_.summary: Sumantra Bose's Kashmir: Roots of Conflict, Paths to Peace traces the dispute from 1846 through the 2002 Indian elections, arguing that durable peace requires recognition of Kashmiri political agency and federal accommodation across the LoC. The book draws on Indian, Pakistani, and Kashmiri sources plus extensive fieldwork. Field sites: Srinagar, Jammu, Azad Kashmir. Methodology: political-historical analysis with interviews. Published 2003 by Harvard University Press.

Sumantra_Bose/Sumantra_Bose_Roots_Confli.author: Sumantra Bose
Sumantra_Bose/Sumantra_Bose_Roots_Confli.title: Kashmir: Roots of Conflict, Paths to Peace
Sumantra_Bose/Sumantra_Bose_Roots_Confli.summary: Sumantra Bose's 'Sumantra Bose Roots Conflict Paths Peace' is a religious-studies monograph on ethnicity and identity politics, politics and conflict, and religion and ritual. Regional focus: Pakistan. Field site: Jammu, Srinagar, Poonch District, Ladākh. Published 2003.

Max_Klimburg/Klimburg_Kafirs_Hindu_Kush_.author: Max Klimburg
Max_Klimburg/Klimburg_Kafirs_Hindu_Kush_.title: The Kafirs of the Hindu Kush: Art and Society of the Waigal and Ashkun Kafirs
Max_Klimburg/Klimburg_Kafirs_Hindu_Kush_.summary: Max Klimburg's The Kafirs of the Hindu Kush documents the ritual, art, and material culture of the pre-Islamic Kafir communities of the Waigal and Ashkun valleys of Nuristan, drawing on Klimburg's fieldwork before the Afghan wars. The two-volume work catalogues wooden effigies, dance ritual, and lineage organization. Field sites: Waigal and Ashkun valleys, Nuristan, Afghanistan. Methodology: ethnography combined with art-historical documentation. Published 1999 by Franz Steiner.

Akbar_S_Ahmed/Akbar_Ahmed_Pakistan_Socie.author: Akbar S. Ahmed
Akbar_S_Ahmed/Akbar_Ahmed_Pakistan_Socie.title: Pakistan Society: Islam, Ethnicity, and Leadership in South Asia
Akbar_S_Ahmed/Akbar_Ahmed_Pakistan_Socie.summary: Akbar S Ahmed's 'Akbar Ahmed Pakistan Society' is a religious-studies article on ethnicity and identity politics, kinship and family, and politics and conflict. Regional focus: Pakistan. From the opening: 'The answers may help us understandthe tension between traditionand modernityin Muslim society in these last decades of the twentieth century.' Field site: Waziristan, Kano, Wana, Swat. Published 2014.

Mona_Bhan/Bhan_Counterinsurgency_Democra.author: Mona Bhan
Mona_Bhan/Bhan_Counterinsurgency_Democra.title: Counterinsurgency, Democracy, and the Politics of Identity in India
Mona_Bhan/Bhan_Counterinsurgency_Democra.summary: Mona Bhan's Counterinsurgency, Democracy, and the Politics of Identity in India is an ethnography of Brogpa Buddhist communities in Ladakh's Dah-Hanu region, where Indian counterinsurgency doctrine meets Aryan-tourism economy. Bhan argues that 'tribal authenticity' is mobilized by the state to incorporate borderland populations into national identity while justifying military presence. Field site: Dah-Hanu and Drass, Ladakh. Methodology: ethnographic fieldwork. Published 2014 by Routledge.

Haley_Duschinski/Duschinski_Resisting_Oc.author: Haley Duschinski
Haley_Duschinski/Duschinski_Resisting_Oc.title: Duschinski Resisting Occupation Kashmir
Haley_Duschinski/Duschinski_Resisting_Oc.summary: Haley Duschinski's 'Duschinski Resisting Occupation Kashmir' is a historical article on ethnicity and identity politics, gender and women's experience, and politics and conflict. Regional focus: Pakistan, Afghanistan. From the opening: 'In this sense, the volume traces the linkages among colonialism, militarization, power, democracy, and sovereignty and how these play out through control strategies that dominate occupied landscapes.' Field site: Jammu, Srinagar, Ladākh, Shuhadā. Published 2017.

Sahar_Ghumkhor/Ghumkhor_Political_Psycho.author: Sahar Ghumkhor
Sahar_Ghumkhor/Ghumkhor_Political_Psycho.title: Ghumkhor Political Psychology Veil
Sahar_Ghumkhor/Ghumkhor_Political_Psycho.summary: Sahar Ghumkhor's 'Ghumkhor Political Psychology Veil' is a religious-studies monograph on gender and women's experience, politics and conflict, and religion and ritual. Regional focus: Pakistan, Afghanistan. From the opening: 'The Palgrave Studies in Political Psychology book series profiles a range of innovative contributions that investigate the leading political issues and perspectives of our time.' Field site: Soler, Kākar, Kabul. Published 2020 by Palgrave Macmillan.

Tania_Saeed/Tania_Saeed_Islamophobia__53.author: Tania Saeed
Tania_Saeed/Tania_Saeed_Islamophobia__53.title: Islamophobia and Securitization: Religion, Ethnicity and the Female Voice
Tania_Saeed/Tania_Saeed_Islamophobia__53.summary: Tania Saeed's 'Tania Saeed Islamophobia' is a religious-studies monograph on ethnicity and identity politics, gender and women's experience, and kinship and family. Regional focus: Pakistan. From the opening: 'Said 1994; Meer and Modood 2010; Croft 2012) primarily focuses on the male; women are reduced to a phys- ical embodiment of the quintessential ‘victim’.' Field site: Lahore District, Karachi, Peshawar Division, Mirpur District. Published 2016 by Palgrave Macmillan.

Charles_Lindholm/Charles_Lindholm_Genero.author: Charles Lindholm
Charles_Lindholm/Charles_Lindholm_Genero.title: Generosity and Jealousy: The Swat Pukhtun of Northern Pakistan
Charles_Lindholm/Charles_Lindholm_Genero.summary: Charles Lindholm's Generosity and Jealousy is an ethnography of Yusufzai Pukhtun social structure in Swat, Pakistan, drawing on long fieldwork in the late 1970s. Lindholm argues that the ostensible egalitarianism of Pukhtun lineage competition is sustained by intense distrust between agnatic cousins, with hospitality as its public counterpoise. Field site: Swat valley, Pakistan. Methodology: long-term ethnographic fieldwork. Published 1982 by Columbia University Press.

Aisha_Khan/Islam_and_the_Americas__aa605.author: Aisha Khan
Aisha_Khan/Islam_and_the_Americas__aa605.title: Islam and the Americas
Aisha_Khan/Islam_and_the_Americas__aa605.summary: Aisha Khan's 'Islam and the Americas' is a religious-studies monograph on ethnicity and identity politics, gender and women's experience, and kinship and family. Regional focus: Pakistan. From the opening: 'Democracy, Gender, and Indian Muslim Modernity in Trinidad Gabrielle Jamela Hosein 12.' Field site: Karam, Lahore District. Published 2017 by Aisha Khan.

Ananya_Jahanara_Kabir/Kabir_Kashmir_Terr.author: Ananya Jahanara Kabir
Ananya_Jahanara_Kabir/Kabir_Kashmir_Terr.title: Territory of Desire: Representing the Valley of Kashmir
Ananya_Jahanara_Kabir/Kabir_Kashmir_Terr.summary: Ananya Jahanara Kabir's 'Kabir Kashmir Territory desire' is a historical monograph on ethnicity and identity politics, kinship and family, and politics and conflict. Regional focus: Pakistan, Afghanistan. From the opening: 'I would like to acknowledge, first, Mrinal Dasgupta, Khairanara Kabir, and Zuglul Kabir, who put aside legitimate concerns about my safety to support my convictions.' Field site: Srinagar, Jammu, Jhelum District, Ladākh. Published 2009 by Agha Shahid Ali.

Ananya_Jahanara_Kabir/Territory_of_Desir.author: Ananya Jahanara Kabir
Ananya_Jahanara_Kabir/Territory_of_Desir.title: Territory of Desire: Representing the Valley of Kashmir
Ananya_Jahanara_Kabir/Territory_of_Desir.summary: Ananya Jahanara Kabir's 'Territory of Desire Kashmir' is a historical monograph on ethnicity and identity politics, kinship and family, and politics and conflict. Regional focus: Pakistan, Afghanistan. From the opening: 'I would like to acknowledge, first, Mrinal Dasgupta, Khairanara Kabir, and Zuglul Kabir, who put aside legitimate concerns about my safety to support my convictions.' Field site: Srinagar, Jammu, Jhelum District, Ladākh. Published 2009 by Agha Shahid Ali.

Anna_Larson/Larson_Afghanistan_democracy.author: Noah Coburn
Anna_Larson/Larson_Afghanistan_democracy.title: Derailing Democracy in Afghanistan: Elections in an Unstable Political Landscape
Anna_Larson/Larson_Afghanistan_democracy.summary: Noah Coburn (Bennington College) and Anna Larson's joint ethnography of post-2001 Afghan elections, published 2013 by Columbia University Press. The book argues that internationally-funded elections, instead of democratising Afghanistan, entrenched local strongmen and produced a brittle 'electoral landscape' that international donors badly misread. Field sites: Kabul; Istalif (Shomali Plain); Hazarajat; and provinces across Balkh, Logar, and Ghazni during the 2009 presidential and 2010 parliamentary elections. Methodology: multi-sited ethnographic fieldwork in polling stations, campaign offices, and tribal councils, plus elite interviews.

Ayaz_Qureshi/AIDS_in_Pakistan_Bureaucrac.author: Ayaz Qureshi
Ayaz_Qureshi/AIDS_in_Pakistan_Bureaucrac.title: AIDS in Pakistan: Bureaucracy, Public Goods and NGOs
Ayaz_Qureshi/AIDS_in_Pakistan_Bureaucrac.summary: Ayaz Qureshi's 'AIDS in Pakistan Bureaucracy Public Goods and NGOs1' is an ethnographic monograph on agrarian and pastoral life, gender and women's experience, and kinship and family. Regional focus: Pakistan, Afghanistan. From the opening: 'Today you give me syringes, tomorrow you might come and handcuff me’, protested Kamal, the Chief Executive Officer of Naya Sewaira, the biggest NGO in Pakistan’s HIV/AIDS sector.' Field site: Lahore District, Gujrāt District, Karachi, Balochistan. Published 2018 by Palgrave Macmillan.

Ayaz_Qureshi/Multiple_Risks_Among_Male_a.author: Ayaz Qureshi
Ayaz_Qureshi/Multiple_Risks_Among_Male_a.title: Multiple Risks Among Male and Transgender Sex Workers in Pakistan
Ayaz_Qureshi/Multiple_Risks_Among_Male_a.summary: Ayaz Qureshi's 'Multiple Risks Among Male and Transgender Sex Workers in Pakistan' is an ethnographic article on gender and women's experience. Regional focus: Pakistan. From the opening: 'Taylor & Francis makes every effort to ensure the accuracy of all the information (the “Content”) contained in the publications on our platform.' Field site: Rawalpindi Division, Abbottabad, Karachi. Published 2015 by Routledge.

Ayaz_Qureshi/Uncivil_society_the_politic.author: Ayaz Qureshi
Ayaz_Qureshi/Uncivil_society_the_politic.title: Uncivil society the politics of HIV activism in Pakistan
Ayaz_Qureshi/Uncivil_society_the_politic.summary: Ayaz Qureshi's 'Uncivil society the politics of HIV activism in Pakistan' is an ethnographic article on gender and women's experience, kinship and family, and politics and conflict. Regional focus: Pakistan. From the opening: 'Association of the People Living with HIV in Pakistan, established under the auspices of UNAIDS, international NGOs, and the government’s AIDS control department as an attempt to strengthen ‘civil society’.' Field site: Lahore District, Karachi. Published 2014.

Aziz_A_Hakimi/Getting_savages_to_fight_b.author: Aziz Hakimi
Aziz_A_Hakimi/Getting_savages_to_fight_b.title: Getting savages to fight barbarians counterinsurgency and the remaking of Afghanistan
Aziz_A_Hakimi/Getting_savages_to_fight_b.summary: Aziz A Hakimi's 'Getting savages to fight barbarians counterinsurgency and the remaking of Afghanistan' is a religious-studies article on ethnicity and identity politics, politics and conflict, and religion and ritual. Regional focus: Afghanistan. From the opening: 'Yet, as Duffield reminds us, there are larger interests at play in protecting and cultivating tradition; ‘securing the “traditional” and maintaining its cohesion’, he argues, ‘is essential for defending the “modern”’(2005, 148).' Field site: Kabul. Published 2015 by Routledge.

Aziz_A_Hakimi/Good_men_don_t_elope_Afgha.author: Aziz Hakimi
Aziz_A_Hakimi/Good_men_don_t_elope_Afgha.title: Good men don t elope Afghan migrant men s discourses on labour migration marriage and masculinity
Aziz_A_Hakimi/Good_men_don_t_elope_Afgha.summary: Aziz A Hakimi's 'Good men don t elope Afghan migrant men s discourses on labour migration marriage and masculinity' is an economic article on ethnicity and identity politics, gender and women's experience, and kinship and family. Regional focus: Afghanistan. From the opening: 'Writing about the contemporary Middle East, Ghannam argues that ‘work (and there- fore providing) is part of an ethics of care’, and that providing for one’s family ‘is key to a proper working-class man’ (Ghannam 2018, 130).' Field site: Kabul, Khamyāb, Hazāras. Published 2021.

Aziz_A_Hakimi/He_Should_Learn_That_He_Ca.author: Aziz Hakimi
Aziz_A_Hakimi/He_Should_Learn_That_He_Ca.title: He Should Learn That He Cannot Get a Woman for free Male Elopers and Constructions of Masculinity in the Afghan J
Aziz_A_Hakimi/He_Should_Learn_That_He_Ca.summary: Aziz A Hakimi's 'He Should Learn That He Cannot Get a Woman for free Male Elopers and Constructions of Masculinity in the Afghan J' is a religious-studies article on ethnicity and identity politics, gender and women's experience, and kinship and family. Regional focus: Afghanistan. From the opening: 'Abstract This article explores constructions of gender, masculinity, and class in moral crimes prosecutions, and their legal aftermaths in Afghanistan.' Field site: Kabul. Published 2020.

Biao_Xiang/Global___Body_Shopping____An_.author: Biao Xiang
Biao_Xiang/Global___Body_Shopping____An_.title: Global "Body Shopping": An Indian Labor System in the Information Technology Industry
Biao_Xiang/Global___Body_Shopping____An_.summary: Biao Xiang's 'Global: Body Shopping: — An Indian Labor System in the Information Technology Industry' is an economic monograph on ethnicity and identity politics, kinship and family, and politics and conflict. Regional focus: Pakistan. From the opening: 'Agency for International Development VC venture capitalists VHP Vishwa Hindu Parishad (World Hindu Council) WTO World Trade Organization Y2K year 2000 Currencies AUD Australian dollar.' Field site: Hyderabad, Lakh. Published 2007 by Princeton University Press.

C_Sivaramamurti/AMARAVATI_SCULPTURES_IN_.author: Calambur Sivaramamurti
C_Sivaramamurti/AMARAVATI_SCULPTURES_IN_.title: Amaravati Sculptures in the Chennai Government Museum

Conrad_Schetter/Local_Politics_Afghanist.title: Local Politics in Afghanistan: A Century of Intervention in the Social Order

Schetter argues that 'the local' is produced through these interventions rather than existing prior to them. Field sites: rural Afghanistan (Kandahar, Balkh, Kunduz, Bamyan). Methodology: edited political-ethnographic essays. Published 2013 by Hurst.

Adam_Baczko/Taliban_Courts_in_Afghanista.author: Adam Baczko
Adam_Baczko/Taliban_Courts_in_Afghanista.title: The Taliban Courts in Afghanistan: Waging War by Law
Adam_Baczko/Taliban_Courts_in_Afghanista.summary: Adam Baczko's English-language reworking (translated by Henry W. Randolph) of his 2021 La Guerre par le Droit, published by Oxford University Press in 2023. The book argues that the Taliban built sustained popular legitimacy in rural Afghanistan by running parallel sharia courts that resolved everyday land, inheritance, and water disputes more reliably than Karzai-era state institutions. Field sites: rural districts of Wardak, Kunar, Kandahar, Logar, Ghazni; with secondary work among Afghan refugees in Quetta, Pakistan. Methodology: long-term ethnographic fieldwork (2010–2018) with disputants, judges, and former Taliban personnel, plus archival reconstruction of the Taliban judiciary's emergence.

Zoha_Waseem/Insecure_Guardians_Everyday_.author: Zoha Waseem
Zoha_Waseem/Insecure_Guardians_Everyday_.title: Insecure Guardians: Enforcement, Encounters and Everyday Policing in Postcolonial Karachi
Zoha_Waseem/Insecure_Guardians_Everyday_.summary: Zoha Waseem's ethnography of the Karachi Police, published 2022 by Hurst (London) and Oxford University Press. Based on multi-year fieldwork inside police stations, encounter sites, and ranger compounds, the book argues that policing in Karachi is an inherently insecure profession: officers are simultaneously agents and victims of routinised violence, embedded in a postcolonial security apparatus shaped by Sindh's ethnic politics, MQM-era extrajudicial encounters, and the post-2013 Karachi Operation. Field sites: Karachi (Lyari, Malir, Korangi, North Nazimabad). Methodology: ethnography, life-history interviews with constables and officers, archival policing-record analysis. Developed from her King's College London PhD.

Humeira_Iqtidar/Secularizing_Islamists_J.author: Humeira Iqtidar
Humeira_Iqtidar/Secularizing_Islamists_J.title: Secularizing Islamists? Jama'at-e-Islami and Jama'at-ud-Da'wa in Urban Pakistan
Humeira_Iqtidar/Secularizing_Islamists_J.summary: Humeira Iqtidar's monograph (University of Chicago Press, 2011, South Asia Across the Disciplines series) argues counter-intuitively that two prominent Islamist organisations — Jama'at-e-Islami and Jama'at-ud-Da'wa — have been agents of secularisation in urban Pakistan, professionalising religion through bureaucratic structures, mass media, and welfare provision rather than restoring an organic religious order. Field sites: Lahore neighbourhoods (Krishan Nagar, Iqbal Town, Township) and Markaz-e-Tayyaba in Muridke, with secondary observation in Karachi. Methodology: ethnographic fieldwork (2003–2008), party document analysis, interviews with cadres and sympathisers.

Anna_Larson/Power_and_Authority_in_Afgha.author: Anna Larson
Anna_Larson/Power_and_Authority_in_Afgha.title: Power and Authority in Afghanistan: Rethinking Politics, Intervention and Rule
Anna_Larson/Power_and_Authority_in_Afgha.summary: An edited volume from Anna Larson (Tufts/AIIS), Dipali Mukhopadhyay (Minnesota), and Omar Sharifi (Boston University), published 2025 by I.B. Tauris/Bloomsbury. Twelve chapters by Afghan and international scholars rethink power and political authority in Afghanistan after the 2021 Taliban return, arguing that 'intervention' and 'rule' need to be re-theorised away from Western state-building templates. Field sites: Kabul, Kandahar, Bamiyan/Hazarajat, Mazar-e Sharif, Herat, Logar, and the Pakistani borderlands of Quetta and Peshawar. Methodology: edited ethnographic and historical-political case studies; the editors' own chapters draw on long-term fieldwork stretching back to the post-2001 reconstruction era.

Salma_Bibi/Gendered_Landscape_of_Justice.author: Salma Bibi
Salma_Bibi/Gendered_Landscape_of_Justice.title: The Gendered Landscape of Justice: Institutional Barriers to Women's Khula Rights in District Courts Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
Salma_Bibi/Gendered_Landscape_of_Justice.summary: Salma Bibi (PhD scholar, Department of Social Work, University of Peshawar) and Shakeel Ahmed analyse how patriarchal gatekeeping inside Peshawar's district family courts blocks women from invoking their Islamic right to khula (judicial divorce). Field site: Peshawar District family courts and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa civil society. Methodology: qualitative interviews with female litigants, lawyers, and judges, framed by feminist structural-oppression theory (Maeve McKeown). Published 2025 in the Journal of Social Sciences Review 5(1):267–276.

Rahat_Ullah/Access_to_Justice_in_Land_Di.author: Rahat Ullah
Rahat_Ullah/Access_to_Justice_in_Land_Di.title: Access to Justice in Land Disputes: Unveiling Public Challenges in Peshawar Courts
Rahat_Ullah/Access_to_Justice_in_Land_Di.summary: Rahat Ullah (LLM, Kohat University) and Salma Bibi (PhD, University of Peshawar) diagnose why land-dispute litigation in Peshawar's civil and revenue courts drags on for years and erodes public trust. Field site: civil and revenue courts of Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Methodology: qualitative analysis of 30 purposively selected respondents — judges, revenue officers, senior advocates, and litigants — to map the structural, procedural, and administrative barriers to timely justice under the West Pakistan Land Revenue Act 1967 and the Code of Civil Procedure 1908. Published 2025 in Social Science Review Archives 3(4).

Ghazala_Hassan_Qadri/A_Muslim_Womans_Rig.author: Ghazala Hassan Qadri
Ghazala_Hassan_Qadri/A_Muslim_Womans_Rig.title: A Muslim Woman's Right to a Khul' in Pakistan: Marital Relief or Marital Pain?
Ghazala_Hassan_Qadri/A_Muslim_Womans_Rig.summary: Ghazala Hassan Qadri's PhD thesis (University of Birmingham, Department of Theology and Religion, submitted November 2016, accepted 2017) re-examines the Hanafi jurisprudence of khul' — the woman-initiated divorce — and tracks its translation into the Pakistani legal system. Qadri argues that earlier scholarship misread Hanafi fiqh as requiring the husband's consent and a financial penalty, and shows how Pakistani courts have effectively created a no-fault khul' through judicial activism. Field site: Lahore family courts. Methodology: doctrinal fiqh analysis, statutory review, plus qualitative interviews and participant observation with female litigants and judges in Lahore.

Shabana_Shamaas_Gul_Khattak/Voices_of_th.author: Shabana Shamaas Gul Khattak
Shabana_Shamaas_Gul_Khattak/Voices_of_th.title: Voices of the Unvoiced: Women's Struggle for Education in Khyber Pukhtunkhwa, Pakistan
Shabana_Shamaas_Gul_Khattak/Voices_of_th.summary: Shabana Shamaas Gul Khattak's book-length study of women's pursuit of formal education across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, published 2025 by Anthem Press (London/New York; distributed via Cambridge Core). The book documents how Pashtun gender norms, post-9/11 militancy, the 2009 Swat displacement, and KP's underfunded public schools combine to produce structural barriers — and how local women, teachers, and NGOs work around them. Field sites: Swat, Peshawar, Mardan, Charsadda, and Malakand division. Methodology: feminist ethnography, oral histories with school-girls, mothers, and women teachers, plus local-government archival work.

Maira_Hayat/Storage_as_Security_Damming_.author: Maira Hayat
Maira_Hayat/Storage_as_Security_Damming_.title: Storage as Security: Damming Water in Pakistan
Maira_Hayat/Storage_as_Security_Damming_.summary: Maira Hayat's short essay in Political Geography (2022) examines how Pakistani elites — including former Chief Justice Saqib Nisar — frame large dam construction (Diamer-Bhasha, Mohmand, Mangla, Tarbela) as a moral and security imperative against Indian water-bombing fears. Field site: Lahore (engineering academies); analytic site: Pakistan's dam infrastructure on the Indus. Methodology: ethnographic vignettes and discourse analysis of public-fundraising appeals. Published 2022 in Political Geography 97 (Suppl C), DOI 10.1016/j.polgeo.2022.102629.
